- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for the following 5-day horizon.
- If sentiment is negative or mixed (≤0.3), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment is erratic.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 18-day mean is > forecast, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5%.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00s), model may overfit to recent highs; cap forecast at 1.5–2% above recent 18-day high.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days, then allow gradual reversion.
